status.label: Design candidate
status.detail: The original report says Keyboard Manager shortcut enablement reverts after closing Settings. A later user describes remaps that appear enabled but stop working, with toggling restoring them. These symptoms may share state persistence/application but the responsible path is unconfirmed.

next_action: Reproduce setting persistence and runtime remap-state behavior separately on a current build.

actions.note: Queues the design workflow for maintainer approval; no upstream write occurs.
actions.label: Review Keep Keyboard Manager enablement consistent across UI and runtime

steps: Enable the reported setting, close/reopen Settings, and record whether it remains enabled.
Separately test the Chrome-limited remaps; if one stops working while shown enabled, toggle it once and compare.
prerequisites: Use a non-critical test remap and preserve settings.
For second scenario use the reported Chrome-limited Ctrl+W and Ctrl+Shift+P mappings if available.
reproduce.expected_result: Persisted toggle state and actual runtime remap behavior match.
reproduce.version_requirements: Current supported build; include v0.100.2 scenario only if available

judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce setting persistence and runtime remap-state behavior separately on a current build.
evidence: Original steps: toggle shortcuts to programs on, close Settings, reopen; setting is off.
A 2026-10-16 v0.100.2 report says disabled remaps sometimes stop working while shown enabled; toggling restores them.
The later report involves two Chrome-limited remaps and does not confirm the same cause.
judgment.rationale: The original report says Keyboard Manager shortcut enablement reverts after closing Settings. A later user describes remaps that appear enabled but stop working, with toggling restoring them. These symptoms may share state persistence/application but the responsible path is unconfirmed.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys code change is plausible; uncertainty and confidence are stated in the proposed plan.

verification: Verify global enablement persists through Settings reopen and runner restart.
Verify remaps function and the UI accurately reflects runtime state.

confidence.rationale: The symptoms are concrete, but reports cover different toggles without a shared confirmed cause.

plan: Reproduce global shortcut toggle and compare its value before and after reopening Settings and restarting the runner.
Separately reproduce Chrome-limited remap failure and compare persisted configuration with runtime state.
Trace the confirmed divergence; unify causes only if evidence supports it.
Fix the confirmed state boundary and add regression tests.
proposed_fixes.title: Keep Keyboard Manager enablement consistent across UI and runtime
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Red hypothesis: configuration may not persist or apply consistently to the runtime engine; toggle reversion and intermittently inactive mappings may be separate faults.

issue_context.analysis: Two actionable observations exist but no source-grounded cause. Reproduce independently before implementation; do not assume the per-remap report is the same defect.
initial_investigation: Reviewed original steps, attached UI screenshots, and latest comment describing intermittent per-remap behavior.
No linked fix PR or duplicate was established.
inferences: The UI setting and runtime enablement could diverge, but a shared persistence cause is unconfirmed.
known_information: The issue says the enable/disable toggle is Off again after reopening Settings.
A separate recent commenter reports disabled remaps stop working while the UI shows enabled.
The latest report specifies two Chrome-limited mappings and PowerToys 0.100.2.
issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager shortcut enablement may not persist or may desynchronize from runtime state; current reports do not establish whether these are one defect.

title: Keyboard Manager isn’t saving the shortcut enable/disable toggle.
